problem_text:
A logistics firm must devise a procurement and storage schedule for a critical component across an 11-week operational window.  
The starting stock at the outset of the planning interval is 20 units.  
In each week \(t = 1, \dots, 11\), the vendor permits the firm to issue a purchase requisition whose amount must fall between 5 and 69 units.  
Nevertheless, every requisition placed will require 1 week(s) for delivery before it becomes available to meet requirements or augment stock.  
The requirement for the component in each week is specified as follows:  
* Week 1: requirement 43 units  
* Week 2: requirement 50 units  
* Week 3: requirement 28 units  
* Week 4: requirement 12 units  
* Week 5: requirement 10 units  
* Week 6: requirement 34 units  
* Week 7: requirement 31 units  
* Week 8: requirement 20 units  
* Week 9: requirement 45 units  
* Week 10: requirement 54 units  
* Week 11: requirement 19 units  

Stock‑outs are tolerated, but any unsatisfied requirement will not be carried forward.  
Throughout the planning horizon, component quantities may be fractional, and the total quantity of physical stock on hand at any moment must not surpass the storage facility’s limit of 48 units.  

In week 10, the maximum permissible requisition size is 47 units.  
In week 1, the physical stock on hand must be no less than 30 units.  

The aggregate expense over the planning horizon comprises three elements: the procurement expense, which amounts to 6 per unit requisitioned; the storage expense, which amounts to 3 per unit of stock held from one week to the next; and the shortage penalty, which amounts to 9 per unit of unfulfilled requirement. Determine the optimal requisition quantity for each week and monitor the consequent stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the total expense.
